title: The addressability boundary was partly self-imposed

the_correction.r84_said: '129 of 130 MiniWob families expose no code-readable terminal state'
the_correction.wrong_because: MiniWob's own scorer reads WOB_DONE_GLOBAL and WOB_REWARD_GLOBAL through Runtime.evaluate. The terminal state was ALWAYS readable as code.
the_correction.what_made_it_unreadable: the r82 decision to forbid Runtime.evaluate in the vision channel. Right for ACT, wrong for VERIFY.

split.act: pixels and input events only, unchanged
split.verify: typed read-only state questions with a data-only selector

channel_safety.selector_guard: a selector containing ; => ( ) { } = ` \ eval function constructor is refused, so a read can never become an execution

two_input_defects_found_by_using_it.symptom: typing into a listener-bound field left it EMPTY while elementFromPoint confirmed the click landed on the right node
two_input_defects_found_by_using_it.cause: type_text sent only Input.dispatchKeyEvent{type:char}; no keyDown, so no input event
keyDown carrying a `text` field inserts the character, and the following `char` inserts it again

planner_findings.fixed: plan_to_reveal returned NO_ROUTE on an EMPTY capability library -- a refusal dressed as a judgement. Now NOT_LOOKED.
planner_findings.self_correction: an independent check of mine read NO_ROUTE from a perfectly good planner because I used the wrong capability dict shape (pre/add/del instead of requires/provides). The planner was not broken; my test was.

suite.honest_read: the typing fix changed nothing measurable; the planner was never the bottleneck because it was almost never invoked

the_real_limiting_factor: The answer is not in the goal text and not on screen: it is behind exactly one disclosure. 30 reveal_target tasks yield one quoted literal; 7 are already visible; 12 get NO_ROUTE; the probe loop that would DISCOVER the disclosure is gated behind a first NO_ROUTE and is too shallow. The sequence is: search, then plan -- the loop does plan, then search.
